text:
Matthew Schaefer is the story on Long Island. He's had more headlines than anyone on the team over the last two weeks, from Sportsnaut's "Matthew Schaefer Making Islanders Must-See TV at Only 19" to the New York Post's report on the child support room opened in his late mother Jennifer's name. On the ice he and Logan Stanley have 56 percent of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) in their minutes together.

The team around him is harder to love right now. The Islanders are 7-6-4 and winless in four (0-2-2), outscored 17-9 in that stretch with only 43 percent of the expected goals, so the slide is real. Over the season they've given up chances at a rate of 3.53 expected goals per 60 minutes, and the goaltending has covered for it: 11 goals fewer allowed than expected. Semyon Varlamov has saved 5.0 goals above expected over his last five starts, and Ilya Sorokin was brilliant in Monday's shootout loss in San Jose.

The blue line is the worry. Ryan Pulock is out two to four weeks (Daily Faceoff), and Ben Hutton, signed last week, is now in the lineup. Up front, Victor Eklund is running hot with 7 points in 10 games against 4.6 expected, and the Brayden Schenn, Emil Heineman and Eklund line is 7-1 in goals. Our simulations give the Islanders an 18 percent playoff chance. If the goalies cool off before Pulock is back, that number has room to fall.
headline: Schaefer is the show, the goalies hold it up
